fatal_errors: The proposed initially single-phase CoCrFeMnNi system does not reconstruct the as-cast dual-phase FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy.
High-strain-rate deformation and dynamic grain refinement replace the target intervention of intermediate-temperature thermal aging.

The proposed grain-boundary amorphization/decohesion mechanism omits the target coupling of enhanced L12 ordering, elevated APBE, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
The hypothesis does not predict the decisive ductile-brittle-ductile response, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.

The cited evidence is combined across incompatible regimes: the UHV sliding evidence indicates negligible heating, while the hypothesis invokes elevated-temperature, high-rate deformation as a unified cause.
Local amorphization is asserted without direct support in the supplied evidence.
explanation: The response addresses HEA embrittlement and offers a testable non-segregation alternative, but it reconstructs a fundamentally different material, intervention, structural mediator, and failure mechanism. Its temperature range overlaps the target only superficially. The target concerns aging-induced L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries, with non-monotonic ductility recovery at 750°C; the generated hypothesis instead invokes deformation-induced grain refinement and high-angle-boundary cavitation. The proposed microscopy and mechanical tests could evaluate that alternative, although changing strain rate and temperature simultaneously weakens causal discrimination. Evidence E1 supports intermediate-temperature ductility loss, and E3 cautiously suggests segregation-free boundary decohesion may be possible, but none of the supplied evidence establishes the full dynamic-refinement-to-amorphization mechanism under the proposed elevated-temperature loading conditions.
